subject: Next steps: Private onramp, networking handoff & structured-output plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Alex Lopez <alex@dataforge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps: Private onramp, networking handoff & structured-output plan

Hi Alex — great call today, thanks for walking through your use case and the latency/throughput targets. I wanted to capture the action items and a recommended sequence so we can coordinate your network/security and engineering teams efficiently.

Recap of what we captured on the call
- Deployment mode: Private onramp (VPC endpoint) + optional dedicated pool for production traffic.
- Network: IP allowlist / egress policy; DNS + Route 53-friendly setup; mutual TLS for inbound egress (client cert).
- Auth & SDK: short-term: API key for PoC; long-term: mTLS or workload identity + short-lived tokens for higher security.
- Routing / structured output: you want tool-calling and JSON-structured outputs for downstream orchestration.
- Embeddings & rerank: embeddings produced by Redwood; plan to run a vector rerank pipeline (embed -> kNN -> rerank pass).

What we need from DataForge (please share items below before the handoff call)
1) Network owner & Security lead for the handoff (name + email) — so we can set a meeting with our infra/security engineers.
2) Public IP ranges and existing VPC CIDR(s) you expect to peer/route from (or confirm you'll use VPC endpoint).
3) Typical request QPS and peak tokens per minute for your workload (helps sizing).
4) Any compliance constraints for key exchange (e.g., you require HSM-wrapped certs or internal CA).
5) A sample JSON output schema for the tool-calling flow (if available).

Proposed immediate next steps
- Today/Tomorrow: I’ll send a short checklist and attachment with the recommended VPC endpoint config and IP allowlist template (attached: redwood-connect-checklist.pdf).
- This week: schedule a 45-min technical handoff with DataForge network + security owners and our infra engineer (Karthik).
- Before PoC: Jordan will provide a short SDK snippet for auth options and a sample prompt/structured-output example we recommend.

Attachments included: redwood-connect-checklist.pdf, sample-prompt-outputs.md, mutual-action-plan.xlsx (stubbed).

Would Tuesday or Wednesday this week work for the technical handoff? Alex, if you can point me to the right network contact I’ll coordinate calendars.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Vivek — thanks for the clear recap and checklist. Quick responses:

- Network/security owners: Sara Mendez (sara.m@dataforge.com) will lead the handoff; she owns network and infra. I’m copying her here.
- IP ranges: we run in us-west-2; our egress NAT pool is 34.213.120.0/22 and we have an internal VPC 10.50.0.0/16. If you prefer, we can use a VPC endpoint approach instead of opening NAT egress.
- QPS: baseline 25 QPS with spikes up to ~120 QPS; typical prompt sizes 300-800 tokens, long-form up to 2k for summarization flows.
- Compliance: we prefer mTLS for production; for PoC API key is fine. We do not require HSM for cert storage.
- Sample schema: not formal yet — we can share a rough example in the next email.

I attached our network diagram (df-network-diagram-v1.pdf) — hope that helps.

On the mTLS exchange: do you have an expected cert format (PEM) and rotation guidance? Also — curious whether Redwood supports client cert validation with a presented CN that we can map to project IDs.

Tuesday 11am PT works for us for the handoff — if that’s open for your team we can lock it.

Thanks,
Alex

alex@dataforge.com | +1 (206) 555-0189

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps: Private onramp, networking handoff & structured-output plan

Alex, Vivek — looping in a few technical details so Sara has a concrete expectation for the handoff call. I’m Redwood’s infra lead on private connectivity.

Short answers up front
- VPC endpoint vs egress NAT: both supported. VPC endpoint (privatelink-style) is simpler for customers that want no public egress. If you use NAT egress, we’ll need the public egress IP ranges (you provided already).
- mTLS: we support client certificate validation and can authenticate based on CN or SAN. We accept PEM-encoded certs; for rotation we recommend short-lived certs (90 days) and we can integrate with your internal rotation tooling. If you want to map CN->project IDs we can configure that as part of the endpoint ACL.
- Auth for PoC: API key in header (Authorization: Bearer <key>) is fine. For production we recommend mutual TLS or short-lived tokens issued by your identity provider.

SDK snippet (quick example for the PoC using API key):
- Node (pseudo)
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, baseUrl: 'https://private.redwood.example' });
  const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-13b', input: 'Summarize...', maxTokens: 512 });

For mTLS we expose instructions to configure the client TLS bundle; we’ll verify the client cert on connection.

Structured output & tool-calling
- We support JSON schema enforcement and tool-calling. For your orchestration flows, send a schema that describes the fields the tool expects; our runtime will validate the model output and return structured JSON + provenance.
- For multi-step tool flows we recommend returning: {"tool_request": {...}, "verification": {...}} with a separate traces field for token provenance.

Embeddings & rerank guidance
- Approach: embeddings via Redwood endpoint -> vector store (we can host or you can host) -> kNN candidate set -> rerank with a short-pass generation that uses the candidates.
- Sizing: with your 120 QPS spike and 2k token prompts we recommend a dedicated pool and batching window of 40-60ms to keep latency SLOs while controlling cost.

Attachments referenced: sample-prompt-outputs.md (examples of structured output), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (M.A.P.).

Next for the handoff call
- Please share a network ownership contact (Sara — I see you are on this thread). I’ll bring our network engineer and the VPC endpoint playbook.
- Alex/Vivek — confirm Tuesday 11:00 PT and I’ll drop a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
